_meta.note: Anchor levels + growth rates for the AI Clock (ai-clock.html reads this). 'anchor' is the 'as of' date for the scenario levels. The roll-clock workflow advances the anchor and rolls the levels along their growth curves quarterly, opening a PR; a human then re-anchors against fresh disclosures. Growth rates are human-judged, not scraped.
_meta.reanchor_log: 2026-08-08 (off-cycle, human): capex levels cut ~26% — the 1.77x rate matched big-four guidance exactly but the levels implied a $978B calendar-2026 total vs ~$725B actually guided. Tokens levels roughly doubled — the old anchor tracked Goldman's May 2026 estimate (5.6 quadrillion/month), since superseded by a ~11 quadrillion/month bottom-up run-rate. Energy trimmed to the IEA 2026 figure. Users rate cut 1.5 -> 1.35 as the leaders decelerate. CO2, water, spend, prompts, compute, frontier and unitCost levels left as rolled.
open_questions: tokens rate (5x/yr): near-term observation supports it (Google disclosed 7x YoY at I/O 2026), but forecasts to 2030 imply ~2.2x/yr. Kept at 5 because this model is re-anchored quarterly and is explicitly not for multi-year extrapolation. Revisit each quarter.

co2 levels imply 230/309/433 g CO2/kWh across the three scenarios, i.e. the grid-intensity assumption is part of what the scenarios bracket. This is deliberate — see the CO2 note in ai-clock.html — but it is not independently sourced.
frontier level could not be re-verified: no 2026 record training run is publicly confirmed. Still projected forward from Grok 4 (mid-2025). 'Not disclosed' is the honest state here.
frontier rate is 4.5x/yr; Epoch's central estimate is 5x/yr (CI 4-6x). Within the interval, left unchanged this cycle.
